title: Treatment of Ligament Constructs with Exercise-conditioned Serum: A Translational Tissue Engineering Model
protocol: Maintain sterility and perform all steps in a biological safety cabinet (BSC).
Collect approval from the appropriate ethics review board for the collection and use of human tissues.
Prepare 5x antibiotic/antimycotic (ABAM) solution by diluting 100x ABAM solution in 1X phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Collect ACL tissue fragments in 5X ABAM solution in a 50 mL conical tube, store at 4 °C until the digestion step.
Cut tissue into smaller fragments with a razor blade if necessary to a maximum size of 1 x 1 x 1 cm3.
Prepare a sufficient volume of collagenase solution to submerge the tissue fragments.
Dissolve collagenase type II (1 mg/mL) in high glucose Dulbecco's modified Eagle medium (DMEM) containing 1x penicillin/streptomycin, and 20% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Filter the collagenase solution at 0.22 μm.
Rinse ACL tissue 3 times in PBS.
Transfer ACL tissue to a new 50 mL conical tube and add a sufficient volume of collagenase solution to submerge the tissue.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight (~17 h).
Prepare growth media by supplementing DMEM high glucose media with 10% FBS and 100 U/mL penicillin.
Vortex the tissue-containing 50 mL tube briefly three times every 5 min, starting 15 min before the digestion time is complete.
Triturate the digested tissue vigorously using a 25 mL serological pipette to break up the tissue further and dislodge cells.
Centrifuge at 1,500 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL GM.
Repeat steps 1.8-1.9 three more times.
After the last centrifugation, resuspend the pellet in 5-10 mL GM.
Perform a cell count with a hemocytometer on a small sample of the cell suspension.
Assess cell viability using Trypan Blue.
Plate the cell suspension onto 15 cm tissue culture plates at a density of 3-4 x 10^5 cells per plate.
Culture to 70% confluence in a sterile incubator maintained at 37 °C and 5% CO2, changing GM every three days.
Freeze cells for future use when using or storing within 5 passages.
Trypsinize cells at 70% confluence by aspirating media and washing cells with PBS.
Add enough pre-warmed (37 °C) 0.05% trypsin to just cover the bottom of tissue culture plates.
Place plates in the culture incubator for ~5 min until cells are detached, verifying cell detachment using a light microscope.
Collect detached cells using a pipette and dispense into a Falcon tube.
Centrifuge cells to pellet them.
Resuspend pelleted cells in DMEM high glucose media containing 20% FBS and 10% DMSO.
Aliquot resuspended cell suspension into cryovials.
Cool cryovials at -1 °C/min for at least 24 h.
Store frozen cryovials in liquid nitrogen.
Mix silicone elastomer kit according to manufacturer's instructions.
Dispense approximately 2 ml of silicone per 35 mm tissue culture plate using a 10 mL syringe.
Allow silicone to cure at room temperature for 2-3 days.
Prepare silicone reverse-molds containing cylindrical wells for anchor formation.
Place plastic cylinders in a 35 mm dish with uncured silicone according to desired mold specifications.
Prepare molds: Place one minutien pin in the center of each cylindrical well in the molds.
Combine β-tricalcium phosphate and orthophosphoric/citric acid solution at a 1 g/mL concentration in a plastic weigh boat on ice.
Mix the cement vigorously using a plastic cell scraper.
Triturate the cement to continue mixing.
Pipette mixture into the mold.
Centrifuge the filled mold for 1 min at 2,200 x g.
Allow brushite cement anchors to set at room temperature overnight.
Remove anchors from the mold.
Pin two anchors 12 mm apart in each silicone-coated plate.
Sterilize pinned plates by spraying with 70% ethanol.
Place sterilized plates into a BSC.
Aspirate plates after at least 30 minutes.
Replace lids on aspirated plates.
Store plates in the BSC until needed.
Obtain approval from an ethics review board for the protocol.
Obtain written informed consent from human subjects to participate.
Use a trained phlebotomist to obtain a resting blood sample by venipuncture into an appropriate evacuated container.
Have participants engage in a resistance exercise protocol, consisting of five sets of leg press with one-minute rest between sets.
Perform a set of knee extensions and a set of hamstring curls consecutively without rest.
Repeat the back-to-back exercises three times with 1 min rest between sets.
Collect a post-exercise blood sample 15 min after completing the exercise protocol.
Allow blood to clot before centrifuging at 1,500 x g for 10 min.
Transfer serum to sterile tubes under sterile conditions.
Store serum at 4 °C for future media supplementation.
Store a small aliquot of serum at -20 °C for biochemical analysis.
Form Engineered Ligaments
Expand primary fibroblasts in advance.
Prepare silicone-coated plates with pinned brushite anchors in advance.
Prepare thrombin.
Dissolve bovine thrombin at 200 U/mL in DMEM high glucose media.
Filter the solution at 0.22 µm.
Aliquot and store the thrombin at -20 °C.
Prepare fibrinogen.
Dissolve bovine fibrinogen at 20 mg/mL in DMEM high glucose media.
Incubate for 3-4 h in a 37 °C water bath, swirling every 30 min to aid dissolution.
Filter the solution at 0.22 µm (multiple filters may be needed).
Aliquot and store the fibrinogen at -20 °C.
Prepare aprotinin.
Dissolve aprotinin in water at 10 mg/mL.
Filter the solution at 0.22 µm.
Aliquot and store the aprotinin at -20 °C.
Prepare aminohexanoic acid.
Dissolve aminohexanoic acid in water at 0.1 g/mL.
Filter the solution at 0.22 µm.
Aliquot and store the aminohexanoic acid at 4 °C.
Prepare ascorbic acid.
Dissolve ascorbic acid in DMEM high glucose media at a concentration of 50 mM.
Filter the solution at 0.22 µm.
Store the ascorbic acid at 4 °C.
Prepare L-proline.
Dissolve L-proline in PBS at a concentration of 50 mM.
Filter the solution at 0.22 µm.
Store the L-proline at 4 °C.
Reconstitute TGF-β1 according to the manufacturer's directions at a concentration of 10 µg/mL.
Aliquot and store the TGF-β1 at -20 °C.
Determine the number of constructs required for the experiment.
Ensure sufficient numbers of pinned plates are prepared.
Culture cells in 15 cm plates to achieve 70% confluence.
Trypsinize cells and resuspend in GM at a concentration of 3.67 x 10^5 cells/mL.
Generate a master mix containing 681 µL cell suspension, 29 µL thrombin, 2 µL aprotinin, and 2 µL aminohexanoic acid for each construct.
Mix the master mix well.
Add 714 µL of the master mix to each pinned plate in a 'figure 8' pattern around the brushite cement anchors.
Ensure that the master mix directly contacts the sides of the anchors.
Gently tap each plate to distribute the master mix evenly across the plate.
Quickly add 286 µL fibrinogen dropwise over one plate.
Slide the plate back and forth and side to side in the BSC to distribute the fibrinogen and form cell-embedded fibrin gels.
Place the constructs in a sterile incubator maintained at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Incubate the constructs for at least 15 min to allow polymerization of the fibrinogen.
Prepare sufficient feed media (FM) for 2 mL per construct.
Supplement GM with 200 µM ascorbic acid, 50 µM proline, and 5 ng/mL TGF-β1.
Add 2 mL FM to cover each construct.
Culture the constructs in a sterile incubator maintained at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for a total of 14 days or to the desired endpoint.
Refresh the media every second day with 2 mL FM.
Determine the length and width of the ligament constructs using digital calipers.
Calculate the cross-sectional area of the tissue.
Unpin the ligament construct from the plate.
Place the anchors in reverse molded grips, ensuring the construct is submerged in PBS.
Adjust the distance between the grips to set the length of the construct to its initial length.
Begin the test: strain the construct to failure at a strain rate of 0.4 mm/s (or ~3%/s).
Calculate stress-strain data from load-deformation data.
Quantify mechanical properties of interest, such as maximal tensile load, ultimate tensile strength and modulus.
Remove engineered ligaments from brushite cement anchors.
Dry the constructs at 120 °C for 25 min.
Determine the dry mass of each construct.
Place the constructs into individual 1.5 mL tubes.
Add 200 µL 6 M HCl to each construct.
Boil the constructs at 120 °C in a heating block for 2 h in a fume hood.
Centrifuge the tubes briefly to collect liquid.
Leave the tubes uncapped and evaporate at 120 °C in a heating block for 1.5 h in a fume hood.
Resuspend the resultant pellet in 200 µL hydroxyproline buffer.
Store the resuspended construct at -20 °C until needed.
Prepare hydroxyproline buffer by dissolving 16.6 g citric acid, 4 mL acetic acid, and 11.4 g NaOH in 300 mL water.
Adjust the pH to 6-6.5 and bring the volume up to 500 mL with water.
Add 250 µL toluene as a preservative to the buffer.
Store the buffer at 4 °C protected from light.
Prepare trans-4-Hydroxy-L-proline by dissolving it in water to make a 4 mg/mL solution.
Prepare chloramine-T by dissolving it in water to make a 14.1 mg/mL solution.
Prepare aldehyde-perchlorate by dissolving 1.5 g 4-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde in a mixture containing 6 mL 1-propanol, 2.6 mL perchloric acid, and 0.5 mL water.
Dilute a sample of each resuspended pellet in hydroxyproline buffer to a volume of 200 µL.
Prepare hydroxyproline standards by diluting hydroxyproline in hydroxyproline buffer to 80 µg/mL.
Perform serial dilutions to make 6-8 200 µL standards between 0-20 µg/mL.
Add 150 µL 14.1 mg/mL Chloramine T solution to each standard and diluted sample.
Vortex the solutions.
Incubate at room temperature for 20 min.
Add 150 µL aldehyde-perchlorate solution to each sample and diluted sample.
Vortex the solutions again.
Incubate in a heating block at 60 °C for 15 min.
Dispose of the excess aldehyde-perchlorate solution as hazardous waste according to local regulations.
Allow standards and samples to cool.
Aliquot 200 µL of each standard and diluted sample, in duplicate, into 96-well plates.
Read plate at 550 nm in a spectrophotometer.
Dispose of plate and the remaining volume in 1.5 mL tubes as hazardous waste according to local regulations (contains perchloric acid).
Convert the absorbance value for each sample to micrograms of hydroxyproline using the hydroxyproline standard curve.
Multiply each well by 2.5 to calculate amount of hydroxyproline in the diluted sample.
Recall that only 200 of the 500 µL total mixture is added to each sample well.
Multiply by dilution factor (Section 7.7) to calculate amount of hydroxyproline in original sample.
Divide by 0.137 to calculate the amount of collagen.
Divide by the dry mass to calculate the collagen fraction and convert to a percentage.
Prepare constructs for 3D tissue as per Step 5 above.
Snap-freeze constructs in liquid nitrogen after treatment/intervention.
Grind constructs into powder using a mortar and pestle cooled on dry ice.
Culture human ACL fibroblasts to confluence in DMEM in six-well plates.
Aspirate DMEM and apply treatment media according to experimentation strategy.
Aspirate treatment media and wash cells with PBS.
Scrape cells to collect using an appropriate extraction buffer/reagent.
Use cytosolic extraction buffer (e.g., 250 mM sucrose, 50 mM Tris pH 7.4, 5 mM MgCl2, protease/phosphatase inhibitor cocktail) to obtain protein lysates.
Perform protein concentration assay according to standard procedures.
Continue analysis using western blot procedures.
Isolate total RNA using 500 µL RNA isolation reagent according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Perform reverse-transcription and real-time quantitative PCR analysis according to standard procedures.
Isolate genomic DNA using DNA isolation reagent according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Quantify DNA concentration by measuring the sample absorbance at 260 nm using a spectrophotometer.
